etymologies.etymologyHTML: Partly from Middle French heroïque and partly from Latin hērōicus. By surface analysis, hero +‎ -ic.

definitions.definition: Of or relating to a hero or heroine; supremely noble.

quote.citation: 1928, Franklin D. Roosevelt, The Happy Warrior Alfred E. Smith‎[1], Houghton Mifflin, →OCLC, →OL, page 40:
quote.text: To stand upon the ramparts and die for our principles is heroic. To sally forth to battle and win for our principles is something more than heroic.

quote.citation: 1999, W. Peter Iliff, Varsity Blues, spoken by Mox (James Van Der Beek):
quote.text: Now, we go out there and we half-ass it because we're scared, all we're left with is an excuse. We're always gonna wonder. But, we go out there and we give it absolutely everything… that's heroic.

definitions.definition: (sculpture) Of a size larger than life, but less than colossal.
